original.title: A reverse-source forest injects C events into forward or missing hosts
original.statement: C_a ↪ F_a ⊔ W_a, with each terminal host strictly left of the starting C host.
assumptions: Canonical positive-MEX/COPY recurrence and the named banked lemmas in the source.

exactAuditedStatement: For every mortal owner a there is a source-defined injection C_a to F_a disjoint-union W_a, whose terminal physical host is strictly left of the starting C host. It avoids the p-service at row p-1 and host0. For any integer b<=a, |{C hosts<=b}|+|{reverse hosts<=b}|<=|{P hosts<b}|.
hypotheses: p=sigma_a, y=d(a), P actual predeath p hosts. Reverse hosts have v_y<u_p; forward hosts have u_p<v_y; W has no y service.
proofDependencyMap: Shared canonical foundation: exact positive-MEX/COPY recurrence and P01-P12, independently reconstructed in ../CANONICAL-FOUNDATIONS.md with exact declaration mapping and game interpretation. DEPENDENCIES.json records the additional service lemmas. Final kernel receipts bind the source versions.
FFD, blocker seed exclusion, private nonreuse and rail0.
independentDerivationAndChecks: At a C or reverse y cell, p<y is absent from that host journal: C never books p, reverse books it only later. MEX puts p strictly left in the same row. That source is an actual predeath private p cell because the current row< p.

All domain y cells occupy distinct rows; row injectivity forbids two y cells in one row, and private nonreuse forbids duplicating one host service. Distinct target p cells also have distinct hosts by p nonreuse. Thus the first-source map from C union reverse hosts toP is injective and strictly decreases host.

Each reverse P vertex has one outgoing edge, and every P vertex indegree<=1. C starts are outside P. Finite strictly decreasing host chains cannot cycle or merge from distinct C starts; they terminate at P outside reverse, hence forward or W. A continuation through a reverse target also strictly decreases y source time since its y precedes its current p service.

C starts satisfy t<sigma_h<p, hence t<=p-2. Later steps only decrease source time, so terminal p service is before p-1; rail0 serves p exactly at p-1 and is excluded. The host-prefix inequality follows by restricting the first-source injection, not by assuming terminal F is compensation.
A forward terminal can be a D service after owner death. Therefore this injection does not prove C maps to X/W, A1, or |C|<=|X|+|W|.
